context: Sortable table of 25 D3 skills showing monthly line-count growth over 12 months, with embedded sparklines colored by 7 categories and a change-% column.
first_impression: Clean and scannable — the table structure keeps 25 rows organized and the category color system is consistent, but the sparklines are nearly flat due to a shared global y-scale that spans the full data range.
what_works: The 7-color category palette stays under the perceptual warning threshold and is applied consistently to both dot indicators and sparkline strokes, making category lookup fast. The sortable columns and hover tooltips layer in detail on demand without cluttering the static view.
what_doesnt: The shared global y-domain (globalExtent across all 25 skills) compresses individual growth curves into near-horizontal lines for lower-value skills, defeating the purpose of the sparkline as a trend indicator. At 26px tall, the sparklines are also at the minimum viable height — a few pixels shorter and per-row trends would be unreadable.
